notes.title: Final Demo Patch
notes.content: [p]Hello again, Soulfallen.[/p][p][/p][p]The Early Access launch date is fast approaching, and with it my efforts have shifted almost entirely to the final content additions that I have planned. I am incredibly excited for you all to see what I have in store, I hope to greatly exceed any expectations you may have. In this update post I will be listing some updates/fixes, as well as a general outline of major content planned for the Early Access launch.[/p][p][/p][h3]Updates[/h3][list][*][p]I added an additional boss to the demo slice, making the demo version of the first Act 8 minutes, with 4 demi-bosses[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy ability effects, including better visualizations for area of effect attacks to make dodging more predictable[/p][/*][*][p]Buffing ability damage and reducing cooldown times[/p][/*][*][p]Post-game "damage dealt" screen to show how much damage you did with each damage source to better understand what made your build successful[/p][/*][*][p]Completing quest events now award Marks of Honor, which are now yellow glowing symbols that can be picked up from the ground[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked the enemy AI to improve performance especially with regards to massive groups of enemies (this is more noticable at later stages of each Act, and may not be as noticeable within the first 8 minutes)[/p][/*][*][p]Armor and weapon frames are now stackable, essentially every item in the game is now stackable other than actual weapon or armor pieces, this was done to reduce frustration from inventory clutter[/p][/*][*][p]There are probably a lot more that I'm forgetting, a lot of these are carry-over changes/fixes from my work on the additional 3 Acts[/p][/*][/list][h3]Early Access Launch[/h3][list][*][p]I want everyone to be completely aware of what this game will contain, so I have updated the early access disclosure information on the main store page to comprehensively outline what is expected of the EA launch, and subsequently the 1.0 launch. I will cover most of that here as well[/p][/*][*][p]The game will have 4 Acts, each featuring its own unique biome, environment obstacles, unique enemy types, demi-bosses (each with their own unique abilities), quests, loot, and a final boss[/p][/*][*][p]The duration of each Act will be 20 minutes long, with the exception of Act 4 which is a "race against the clock" mode where 20 minutes is the time cap to reach the end[/p][/*][*][p]There will be 3 base classes, with each class having 3 class specializations, offering different playstyles, different ultimate abilities, and different talent trees[/p][/*][*][p]Each Act has a narrative-drive quest line which is optional, but when completed greatly helps with the difficulty of the final boss fight for each Act[/p][/*][*][p]There are 5 tiers of increasingly rare, powerful, and valuable loot in the form of weapons and armor. Early common items don't help much outside of a bit of extra damage and armor, but higher equipment rarities will give you permanent trait buffs such as increased critical strike chance, or increased base health, allowing for even more build customization[/p][/*][*][p]There will be 12 spellbook abilities, each with 2 upgrade variants, and a final "maxed" ability variant. Each ability has its own level up traits allowing you to create some truly over-powered and enemy-melting builds[/p][/*][*][p]The final Act is a replayable time trial with custom rituals that change each run, challenging you to overcome obstacles, solve problems, and slay a lot of demons before facing your final foe: the Dark Lord[/p][/*][*][p]The Dark Lord boss fight is a lot of fun, and I am so excited for all of you to see it in full and experience it[/p][/*][/list][p]With all of that said, I think I have managed to fit a massive amount of content into this game. I also wanted to mention that for the price of the game I am planning to charge $9.99 USD, with a launch discount of 20% (so roughly $7.99 price at launch). The base price is static and will never increase regardless of updates/expanded content. There will also never be DLC's or any other form of predatory monetization tactics. I think that's all I have for now, this will likely be my last post prior to launch. Exciting times, thank you so much for being along for the ride. [/p]

notes.title: Soulfall Demo Patch 3
notes.content:
[h1][b]It's been a while, Soulfallen.[/b][/h1]

[h2]What's New?[/h2]
While it may have seemed like the game was abandoned due to my lack of updates over the past 3 months, I am extremely excited to announce the largest and most content-filled update I have released so far. In addition to entirely new systems such as skilling, crafting, and talent trees, many of the existing systems have been reworked from the ground up, including Abilities, Level-Up Traits, and enemy scaling. I went back to the drawing board regarding game difficulty and spent a lot of time thinking about what differentiates an unfair/overly punishing game from a difficult, challenging, but ultimately fair one. I believe that I have struck that balance and the result is by far the most fun iteration of Soulfall that has ever existed up to this point. There is really too much new content for me to write about here, so I will list everything below extensively. I strongly encourage you try it out for yourself, you are in for a surprise.

[h2]Feature List[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Western gates of Khelos have finally opened, revealing the resource gathering area. In between your descents into Hell, you can catch fish, mine ore, and harvest plants. These resources can be used to craft weapons, armor, potions, and food that will aid you in your journey and make you more powerful.
[*] Fishing, Mining, Farming, Cooking, Forging, and Alchemy have been fully implemented. These systems introduce dozens of new materials, recipes, and progression mechanics.
[*] Level up traits have been completely re-worked to be more engaging, offer better choice, and make the game more fun with better build variety. 
[*] Abilities gained from Ability Tomes in Hell now have their own traits that can be acquired through leveling up, for example wider Dragon's Breath, more Lightning Strikes, and more Chain Lightning bounces. 
[*] Ultimate abilities have been "removed" and replaced with a new Talent Tree system. You gain talent points by increasing your honor rank, and can spend these talent points to unlock a new and improved version of former "Ultimate Abilities". The general philosophy was to move away from slow charging attacks that force you to stop, and integrate them into the normal gameplay loop.
[*] Instead of charging your Ultimate Abilities, you can choose a talent that gives each attack a percent chance of triggering the Ultimate. This is more fluid, and more fun.
[*] Each class has gained their own class-specific level up traits. Hunter arrows can now ricochet to new enemies, warrior sword swings can now multistrike (triggering two melee swings in rapid succession), and mage spells now have a chance to split into two new projectiles when hitting an enemy.
[*] All abilities have been buffed with higher damage and lower cooldown, among various other tweaks to make each one feel fun.
[*] Enemy damage has been reduced, and enemies have been nerfed in general. Especially formerly devastating boss attacks that could one or two hit kill players, you will find significantly more leniency and what I believe to be more "fair" mechanics.
[*] The character creator has been completely reworked and streamlined to remove a lot of the unnecessary bloat, and simplify the overall process.
[*] A new "Training Mode" has been added, where all enemies have half as much health and deal half as much damage. You cannot acquire weapons/armor, or gain marks of justice in training mode, but it can be a great way to learn a boss's mechanics in a low stress environment where dying is nearly impossible.
[*] You will find sneak peek "Previews" of Acts II, III, and IV, the Infernal Highlands, Frozen Wastes, and Castle of the Dark Lord. These Acts will not be playable in the demo but will be in the full game on release. 
[*] Each Act is 20 minutes long, with a unique boss spawning every 2 minutes to challenge you and stop you in your quest to reclaim your soul, for the purposes of the free demo you will continue to have access to the first 6 minutes of gameplay for the first Act.
[*] Stash tabs have now been implemented, costing GP and allowing for massively increased storage space across your characters.
[*] Gear salvage has been implemented, allowing you to break down duplicate gear for forging materials. The purpose behind this is to remove some of the "RNG" from getting a missing piece of equipment. 
[*] The total build size of the game has been reduced from nearly 5.5GB to under 1.5GB (Windows) and 1.08GB (Linux). Due to a complete restructuring of files and chunks you will likely have to re-download a significant portion of the game, but moving forward updates will be miniscule in comparison.
[*] Trees no longer block the player's vision, using some fancy material occlusion logic, you will see your player at all times, even when you are standing behind a tree.
[*] Gold is now automatically picked up without pressing the "E" key. I did not implement this for other items because I don't want to force the player into cluttering their inventory with items they may not want. 
[*] Attack range now visually increases the size of the punch and sword swing visual effects to reflect the increased hitbox.
[*] When you choose "Quit Game" from the settings menu you can now choose to return to the previous level or quit the game entirely. Quitting from Hell will allow you to return to town, and quitting from town will allow you to return to the menu.
[*] Overall improved user interface to make it more clear to the player which option is selected.
[*] Improved visual effects, performance, sounds, as well as texture and 3D object optimizations.
[/list]

[h2]What's Next?[/h2]
I am hoping to collect some feedback on the relatively large number of changes I've made to the game. There is always room for improvement and iteration so I will continue to do so. In addition, I am working heavily on content development for the 2nd, 3rd, and final Acts of the game, as well as fleshing out the 6 additional class specializations. Having all 4 Acts and all 9 class specializations finished are the final hurdles to releasing the full game. As always please feel free to make a post on the discussions page, or DM me anytime with questions, thoughts, or concerns about the game. Your feedback is valuable and always appreciated. Lastly, I want to wish all of you a very happy (and late) Easter. Christ is Risen, He is King of Heaven, rejoice and be glad. Thanks again, and see you next time.

Sincerely, KCS

notes.title: Soulfall Demo Patch 2
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hello again, Soulfallen.[/b][/h1]

[h2]What's New?[/h2]
Since adding controller and steam deck support I have been almost entirely focused on a fairly major addition to Soulfall, and that is: Class Specializations. Currently there is only one spec available for each class, but this will be expanded to 3 each prior to Early Access release. With these class specs come some new features. Firstly, class-specific traits. It may have seemed strange that each class had identical stats, after all why would a warrior and a mage have the same amount of base armor? With class specs, that is no longer the case. Each class spec also unlocks an Ultimate Ability, which can be used while descended in Hell. Additionally, scribes have assembled a small collection of various texts and placed them in the town library. While the information is currently quite sparse, this will be expanded greatly later on. I will post a full breakdown of changes below for anyone curious:

[h2]Feature List[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Eastern Gates of Khelos have finally opened, revealing ancient and incredible power. The overall "Class System" has been expanded with the addition of specializations, class traits, and ultimate abilities.
[*] 3 New Class Specializations added: Berserker Warrior, Evocation Mage, and Marksman Hunter.
[*] 3 New Ultimate Abilities added: Whrilwind, Aimed Shot, and Inferno Pillar.
[*] Leveling up now creates a "push back radius" from the player, sending enemies backwards and creating a small amount of breathing room.
[*] Several new visual effects, including level up and initial spawn in.
[*] Some sound effects were not correctly categorized and couldn't be adjusted by volume meters, this is now fixed.
[*] "Attack Range" trait was completely reworked so that it now benefits hunters and mages, and not just warriors.
[*] Arrows now have a 25% chance to "break" when hitting each enemy, increasing attack range reduces the chance of the arrow breaking. This is more commonly referred to as "piercing", and the name of the attribute may be updated in the future.
[*] Mage projectile spell explosion radius was reduced slightly for lower tier spells, this explosion radius can now be increased by the "Attack Range" trait.
[*] There was a fairly major bug where purple/epic armor was dropping from the gargoyle statue, this was not intended but I will not be removing any items from player inventories/stashes because that seems unfair. I am only making a note of it here because it may cause some confusion to players as it breaks the natural progression I intend for the game.
[*] Town library added with a lore book and prayer book, this is mostly a test for the system to see if it feels intuitive to players. If it works well then I will continue to use this as a "Lore Delivery" mechanism and expand significantly on the books and their contents.
[*] Slightly reduced the time it takes for XP shards to spawn (33% reduction in spawn time).
[*] Increased the size of the ground indicator for the first Boss's air slam attack, to more accurately and fairly show where the player is safe from taking damage.
[/list]

[h2]What's Next?[/h2]
I struggle between two conflicting desires: to overshare absolutely every plan and idea I have for Soulfall, and to keep the details extremely close to the chest. I am sure the best option is somewhere in the middle, so that's what I will attempt to provide. The next update will contain another major addition: Skilling. I am also working on talent trees (unique for each class spec), and a complete rework/overhaul of the character customizer to streamline it and make it MUCH easier for use while maintaining the depth of customization it provides. As always, your feedback is extremely appreciated and I will continue to address it to the absolute best of my ability. Thanks again, and see you next time.

Sincerely, KCS

notes.title: Soulfall Demo Patch 1.5
notes.content:
Hey everyone, 

I hope you're all having a great start to 2025. I've been keeping myself busy since the last patch, mostly focusing on adding controller and steam deck support. I'm very happy to announce that as of today both features are included in the free demo. The game is fully playable (and very fun) on a steam deck, as verified by my personal testing. I have not gotten a "Verified on Deck" badge from Valve yet but I'm hoping once they have time to review the steam deck build this will be added. In addition to controller and deck support I've also made some minor tweaks here and there, including bug fixes, a change to the inventory system, and more. I will include a full list of changes below. As always, if you run into any issues or concerns please feel free to reach out. 

- The demo is now available for Linux + SteamOS
- Steam Deck compatible (no official Valve seal of approval yet)
- Full native controller support
- Custom modifiable input keybinds
- Opening inventory now also shows the character information screen and a new view
- Quest reward chests now spawn their loot into the world instead of presenting an inventory screen
- Spellbook abilities that used to be dependent on mouse cursor location now no longer rely on a mouse cursor (chain lightning targets a random enemy, and meteor shower falls in front of the player)
- Many more

On a personal note, focusing for so long on controller/deck support has me very eager to get back to work on content updates, so expect the next update to be more content focused. Wishing you all the best in the new year.

Sincerely, KCS

notes.title: Soulfall Demo Patch 1
notes.content:
[h3][b]Greetings, Soulfallen.[/b][/h3]

I have been very busy over the past 2 weeks implementing bug fixes, quality of life changes, and general improvements based on the incredible feedback I have received from you. I can't understate the appreciation I have for anyone who has played this game, and even moreso for those of you who have taken the time to offer feedback, criticisms, observations, etc. As a solo developer these issues can be hard to spot until someone else brings them up, so this really is incredibly valuable. Please do not hesitate to reach out if you find any issues with this current patch. Some of the more notabe changes listed below:

[list]
[*] A mysterious new stranger waits for you at the gates of Hell, talk to him and see what he has to say.
[*] A new boss can be found while descended, offering a chance at more powerful "Tier 2" loot.
[*] A quest has been added that will allow players to obtain a weak starter weapon without relying on RNG.
[*] Audio settings have been fixed, allowing you to change the volume for the music, footsteps, and general SFX.
[*] A "How to play" screen has been added to help explain some concepts that may not be obvious at first.
[*] Controls and "How to play" are now listed under the gameplay settings tab.
[*] Improved spawning of crates, barrels, and shrines to avoid strange collision issues.
[*] Level up bug has been fixed that caused the game to unpause before finishing upgrade selection.
[*] Rank ups now require less marks of justice, as the level up algorithm has been switched from exponential to linear.
[*] Armor values for different class armor types have been updated.
[*] The ground slam indicator has been improved.
[*] Capes, rings, and necklaces have been added to all drop tables.
[*] Keyboard input no longer effects upgrade selection, meaning your character's movement won't get interrupted by a level up.
[*] Upgrade re-roll cost has been added, displayed, and accurately accounted for.
[*] A "close" button has been added to the descend screen, allowing you to back out of a descent if you entered the portal by mistake.
[*] Inventory now automatically closes when you close a supply chest.
[*] Deleting a character now prompts with a secondary window to verify you really want to delete.
[*] Character creation can be exited early, via a "Return" button on the top right.
[*] Several loading screen images have been replaced with higher resolution images.
[*] You can now walk over fallen logs rather than having to jump, and enemies will path over them correctly as well.
[*] Potions dropped from crates are now items that can be picked up and used by clicking, rather than being automatically consumed.
[*] Updated file structure ensuring MUCH smaller update sizes moving forward (sorry this one is so big!)
[*] And many other small tweaks
[/list]

I hope all of you had a very wonderful Christmas, and will have a very fun and safe New Year. Know that I will be hard at work getting the Early Access build of Soulfall ready, and I can hardly contain my excitement thinking about all of the things I still have left to show you. It is not an understatement to say that you have only seen about 5% of what the Early Access will contain. Thank you again for being with me so early on in this journey. Truly, I could not do it without you.

Sincerely, KCS
